Study Information 50.10 Non-Technical Synopsis: (Please provide a brief narrative description of proposal. This should typically be less than 75 words and be easily understood by nonscientists, e.g. We propose to test the effectiveness of a new class of anti- inflammatory drugs against arthritis that develops in the hips of dogs affected by congenital hip dysplasia'): We propose to compare the effect of a newly approved product to control pyrexia and BRD in cattle that is a combination of tulathromycin and ketoprofen with a product with similar claims that is a combination of florfenicol and flunixin meglumine. We plan to measure rectal temperature, prostaglandin synthesis, serum amyloid A concentrations, eye temperature, activity and drug concentrations over a series of timepoints to quantify and compare the duration of effect for these two products in cattle.

50.20 Background (Please provide a concise narrative review of the literature and basis for the study): When the bovine immune system encounters a pathogen, inflammatory mediators initiate systemic changes known as the sickness response which includes pyrexia. Cattle often manifest the sickness response as a result of bovine respiratory disease which is treated with an antibiotic, and may be more attenuated with the addition of an NSAID as well (Toaff-Rosenstein, 2015). It has been established that the co-formulation of ketoprofen with tulathromycin alters the pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic profile of ketoprofen in cattle, resulting in pyrexia being controlled for a longer period of time than with ketoprofen alone (Koster, 2021). Both tulathromycin + ketoprofen and florfenicol + flunixin meglumine have been shown to reduce rectal temperature 6 h post-trt compared to tulathromycin or florfenicol alone (FDA, 2021; Thiry, 2014). However, due to tulathromycin + ketoprofen recently being approved for use in cattle, a comparison of the two combinations of an antimicrobial + NSAID have not been evaluated to determine if one controls pyrexia or inflammatory biomarkers for a longer period than the other.

50.30 Literature Search For Unnecessary Duplication This section is for the reduction requirement for the USDA APHIS 3Rs Alternatives. According to the Animal Welfare Information Center, the 3Rs Alternatives are Reduction, Refinement, and Replacement "of animals used in research, testing, and education." The 3Rs established a scientific approach to ensure that pain and distress of research animals were minimized and/or eliminated via process of ensuring unnecessary duplication of experimentation.

If your proposed activity is part of a formal teaching curriculum and is not research or testing, you may not have to perform a literature search for unnecessary duplication. A non-duplication explanation for teaching projects, can be found at: https://www.k-state.edu/comply/iacuc/resources/protocol- development/teaching-projects/index.html. A literature search for unnecessary duplication is required for all proposed research activities using animals.

Project Description 80.10 Objective/Hypothesis: (briefly state the objective of the study - and, if applicable, the hypothesis to be accepted or rejected): Objective: Compare the duration of effect of tulathromycin + ketoprofen and florfenicol + flunixin meglumine on pyrexia and inflammatory biomarkers in yearling calves
80.20 Materials and Methods

80.30 Experimental Design and General Procedures (succinctly outline formal scientific plan for study): Animal Details: Species, strain, sex, age, weight, number Study Timeline: Arrival of animals, acclimation period, start of study, study time points, end of study Biosample Details: Type, amount, method, location, needle size 12 intact, yearling, male, Holstein calves will be enrolled onto the crossover study. Calves are currently housed at LAHA under IACUC protocol #3904. They will remain at LAHA for the duration of the proposed study. Calves will be inoculated with LPS by subcutaneous injection at a dose of 5 µg/kg at the 0 h timepoint (De Koster, 2021). All 12 calves will first be their own controls with rectal temperatures, IRT images, and blood samples taken via jugular venipuncture to quantify PGE metabolite, serum amyloid A and drug concentrations at 10 study timepoints. Accelerometers will also be placed on their left rear leg for the study duration. Blood will be collected from the jugular vein by venipuncuture using a syringe or vacutainer and a 16 G 1.5 inch needle. The ten study collection timepoints are 0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, 36, and 48 h following inoculation. A 3 week washout period will then occur which has been established as an appropriate endotoxin washout period in horses (Holcombe, 2016). Calves will again be inoculated with LPS by subcutaneous injection at a dose of 5 µg/kg at the 0 h timepoint (De Koster, 2021). Then 6 of the calves will be administered tulathromycin + ketoprofen at the labeled SQ dosage in the neck of 2.5 mg tulathromycin and 3 mg ketoprofen/kg (1.1 mL/100 lb) bodyweight and 6 of the calves will be administered florfenicol + flunixin meglumine at the labeled SQ dosage of 6 mL/100 pounds of bodyweight. Then the study collection timepoints will be repeated at 0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24, 36, and 48 h following inoculation with the same biosamples taken as mentioned above. 80.40 Non-animal Alternatives Considered: (were non-animal alternatives considered - why are they not used?): This study is investigating the effect of two antimicrobial + NSAID products on pyrexia and inflammatory biomarkers in cattle thus non-animal alternatives were not an option. 80.50 Animal Model and Species/Strain Justification: (Explain why animals are needed for your study. 90.10 Justification of Animal Numbers / Data: Analysis: Research, testing, and teaching activities should be designed to provide a statistically significant result with a minimum number of animals. The specific method by which the number of animals was determined must be clearly stated. Statistical techniques and/or power analysis are appropriate in most cases to maximize the usefulness of the data generated from each animal. However, the IACUC acknowledges that the basis for an appropriate justification of animal numbers depends largely on the nature of the study itself. Prior experience and expertise with the model in question may be taken into account as well, but must be carefully documented in the protocol. The cost of the animal should not be considered as the primary justification for the use of a particular species or model. Consultation with a biostatistician or use of statistical software during the design phase of the experiment may be useful. content: 100.30 Replacement Alternatives, and refinements, to Painful Procedures: If you have animals listed in Pain Category D or E above, you must complete the following section. If assistance is needed, please contact Andi Parrish, Dir, Vet Med Library at: 785-532-6006 or aparrish@vet.k-state.edu. Replacement refers to the "equipment, technologies, approaches, and/or procedures that directly replace or avoid the use of animals in experiments by incorporating non-animal methods where they would otherwise have been used." Replacement can be full/absolute replacement avoiding any and all use of animals, or partial/relative replacement where animals are still used to provide tissue, cells, and/or organs but experiments are conducted in vitro. Replacement can also include the use of animals that have been slaughtered for meat or euthanized due to other purposes. The Animal Welfare Act requires that you provide a narrative description of methods used and sources searched to ensure that you have verified that alternatives are not available to prevent unnecessary pain and distress. The Animal Welfare Information Center (AWIC) has a site that gives tips for performing this search https://www.nal.usda.gov/awic/alternatives-literature-searching. Refinement is used to ensure unnecessary pain, suffering, lasting harm, and distress to the animals is minimized and/or eliminated. Refinement aims to improve animal welfare "from housing and husbandry to scientific procedures performed on them." This also includes any drugs that might be listed in the Pain or Distress Alleviation section). In leu of a literature search, you may state in the concise narrative that you consulted with the attending veterinarian to approve the use of drugs listed, animal husbandry and welfare, and/or procedures performed. Animal Monitoring 190.10 Animal Monitoring In order to evaluate potential for pain and/or distress, the KSU IACUC requires an approved plan of how pain or distress will be minimized and documentation of how observations of animals will be recorded. All procedures performed upon an animal should be listed on an Animal Monitoring Plan (AMP) form. The AMP form along with the Animal Observation Record (AOR) detail how you will observe your animals and what actions you will take in order to minimize pain or distress associated with your research project. Examples of procedures needing an AMP include surgical procedure, animals that undergo anesthesia, animals experimentally infected with an infectious disease, experimental vaccination, or animals inoculated with potential tumor forming cells. Exceptions to the use of the AMP and AOR would be simple procedures with minimal physiological effect upon the animal, examples of which include blood collection, or injection of therapeutic drugs. If an AMP is included in your approved IACUC document, it is your responsibility as the PI to assure that the AMP activities will be used as described in the approved protocol. It it is your responsibility to be able to provide documentation for the activities called for in the AMP.
